name: repeat_growth
note: a kind costs its worst severity scaled by 1 + REPEAT_GROWTH·ln(n); sublinear, so the first occurrence dominates

name: co_occurrence_step
note: each distinct kind beyond the first scales the whole deduction by this much, capped at 2.0

name: repeat_cost_is_sublinear
note: no kind's second occurrence costs more than its first, and five occurrences cost strictly less than five firsts — the ln(n) shape read off the function rather than off the docstring. Stated at this granularity on purpose: the marginal cost of the nth occurrence is strictly decreasing in the real-valued deduction, but the score is rounded to an integer before it is returned, so at low severity (weight 1.0) consecutive marginals collapse to the same integer and a strict per-step test would be measuring the rounding, not the rule

name: floor_reached_at_repeats

name: a_lone_signal_needs_implausible_persistence_to_flag
note: below critical severity, one repeating kind needs more than 100 debounced events to reach 'flag'. Stated as a measured bound rather than an impossibility: ln(n) grows without limit, so the guarantee is that a broken camera runs out of interview before it runs out of score, not that it mathematically cannot get there

name: single_critical_score

name: order_independent

name: hardware_fault_scores_below_coaching
note: flaky webcam: 6 no-face scores 83 (clean) while coached: phone + notes + background voice + 2 glances scores 75 (review). True would mean the ordering is inverted — a failing webcam sent for human review while a candidate with a phone, written notes and another voice in the room is marked clean. It measured True against the original per-event deduction (79 vs 86) and measures False against the current per-kind one, which is the repair being re-audited rather than asserted.

name: coaching_reaches_a_human
note: the half of the defect that the ordering alone does not fix: getting the two scores the right way round is worth nothing if the coached candidate is still labelled clean, because the label is what the recruiter reads. Verdict is now 'review'.

name: sustained_absence_cannot_stay_clean
note: a defect introduced by the obvious form of the repair and caught before it shipped. Scoring each kind purely at its worst severity makes persistence free: a candidate with the camera turned to the wall for the whole interview (40 debounced no-face events) scored 88/clean under a bounded-saturation draft, which is a worse failure than the inversion being repaired — a mislabelling became a bypass. The shipped sublinear term puts it at 72/review, the honest verdict for a signal that cannot tell a broken camera from an empty chair.

name: verdict_is_advisory_not_a_penalty
note: why a mis-calibrated c(E) is a reporting defect rather than an unfair-outcome defect, and why the repair above changes no candidate's ranking: c(E) enters the fusion multiplicatively, so a low integrity score shrinks the interview's influence toward the resume prior and can never subtract from what the resume earned. Verified over 2100 (candidate, c(E)) pairs in m5_fusion_audit as s_final_stays_between_resume_and_trusted_score. The candidate was never scored down; the recruiter was shown a misleading label.

name: control_internal_tau_b_before
note: agreement between the controls' own ordering and their competence

name: control_internal_tau_b_after
note: the same agreement after fusion. Higher means the honest candidates were ranked better against each other, not worse — so their absolute rank movement was displacement by corrected neighbours rather than misjudgement of them.

name: control_pairs_order_preserved

name: genuine_misordering_of_controls
note: the complement, and the defensible cost figure. Unlike the false-correction rate above it is invariant to how many candidates were planted with errors, so it does not inflate with the size of the correction the fusion is asked to make.

name: lambda_maximising_tau
note: τ-b 0.7903 at λ = 0.95. Reported as an observation about the sweep, not as a tuned setting: λ was fixed at 0.5 before the sweep was run, and tuning it on the same synthetic cohort that evaluates it would be fitting the test set.

name: collapse_max_abs_score_error
note: largest |S_final - S_resume| over all 100 candidates with c(E) = 0. Exact arithmetic, not a tolerance: trust = 0 makes evidence = S_resume, so the convex combination returns S_resume whatever lambda is.

name: fusion_collapses_to_resume_at_zero_integrity
note: with c(E) = 0 every candidate's fused score equals their resume-only score exactly — the property that stops proctoring noise from being a penalty. Stated about scores, not positions: a candidate can still change place when the candidates around them are re-scored.

name: zero_integrity_ordering_equals_zero_lambda_ordering
note: the like-for-like ranking comparison: discarding the interview by distrusting it (c(E) = 0) and discarding it by weighting it out (lambda = 0) produce the same list, position for position, under the same tiebreaks. This is the ordering form of the collapse.

name: tied_candidates_on_llm_score
note: 97 of 100 candidates share their llm_score with at least one other (largest group 10). The 0-25 integer rubric only has 26 possible values for a 100-candidate cohort, so ties are the normal case, not an edge case.

name: baseline_tiebreak_divergence
note: positions on which the fused ranking at c(E) = 0 differs from resume_only_rank. Every one of these would be a pair tied on llm_score, resolved on ats_score by the baseline and on application_id by the fused ranker. Diagnosing this audit's own earlier failure found the gap and rank() now carries ats_score as its third key, so the two agree exactly; it was 83 positions in this cohort before the key was added. Kept as a measurement because it is a regression test for that agreement, and because the tau-b at c(E) = 0 (0.1701) should now equal the resume-only tau-b (0.1701).

name: s_final_stays_between_resume_and_trusted_score
note: 2100 (candidate, c(E)) pairs — 100 candidates across 21 integrity levels from 0 to 100 — checked against the closed interval between their resume-only score and their fully-trusted fused score. Largest excursion outside it: 2.78e-17. This is the defensible form of 'proctoring noise is not a penalty': losing trust in a recording interpolates a candidate back toward their resume score and can never carry them past it in either direction.

name: interview_score_validity
needs: A model run: N candidates through the full adaptive interview with LLM_PROVIDER=ollama, each transcript independently scored by >=3 human raters, then Fleiss' kappa between raters and Pearson/Spearman between the human mean and the rubric total. Until that exists, the cohort's 'unbiased but noisy' interview model is an assumption, and every recovery rate above is conditional on it.

This is the claim the paper can actually make about direction: under this generative model the fused ranking beats the resume-only ranking on every draw attempted, with the effect size varying by the interval above. It remains a statement about the model, not about real candidates.

name: tau_b_fused_across_seeds

name: ndcg_at_10_gain_across_seeds
note: 95% across-seed interval [0.1257, 0.4514]; positive in 200 of 200 draws. NDCG@10 is the graded top-of-list measure, so this is the one that speaks to the shortlist a recruiter would actually read.

name: lambda_maximising_tau_b_modal_value
source: metrics.m10_stability — λ sweep re-run on every draw
note: the maximising λ landed on 5 distinct grid values across 200 draws; the modal value took 132 of them (66.0%), range [0.8, 1.0]. DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Two reasons this must not become a tuning recommendation: the objective is agreement with a ground truth that only exists because we generated it, and the argmax is a property of the draw. Tuning λ against synthetic truth would be fitting the shipped default to our own simulation.

name: lambda_argmax_is_stable_across_draws
source: metrics.m10_stability — λ sweep re-run on every draw
note: NO — the peak moves across 5 grid values, which settles the question: the single-draw maximum reported in M5 is partly sampling noise and the paper must present the sweep as a sensitivity analysis with no preferred λ.

name: lambda_maximising_tau_b_never_below
source: metrics.m10_stability — λ sweep re-run on every draw
note: across 200 draws the maximising λ never fell below 0.8, so while the exact argmax is unstable the *direction* is not: every draw prefers far more interview weight than the shipped default of 0.5. This is the honest form of the λ finding and it is a two-sided result — it says the shipped default is conservative against this cohort's ground truth, and it says the cohort's ground truth is something we generated, so the correct response is to report the sensitivity and leave the default alone rather than to tune λ against our own simulation. A real λ recommendation needs real candidates with human-adjudicated competence.

name: quantities_too_unstable_to_report_from_one_draw
note: MRR and precision@10 are computed from the identity of a handful of top-10 positions, so one swap moves them a long way. The shipped draw reports mrr_fused = 1.0, which reads as a perfect result; the across-seed interval is [0.3333, 1.0]. These two must be reported with their intervals or not at all. τ-b and NDCG@10 are stable enough to quote (widths tau_b_fused 0.1007, ndcg_fused 0.0593).

name: shipped_seed_is_a_representative_draw
source: metrics.m10_stability — shipped value vs across-seed interval
note: all 10 headline quantities from seed 20260923 fall inside their own 95% across-seed interval, so the draw the paper reports is typical of the generator rather than a favourable one. Worth stating explicitly: the seed was fixed before any of these numbers were computed, and this check is what makes that claim verifiable rather than merely asserted.

name: hidden_gem_places_gained
source: metrics.m10_stability — paired bootstrap on the shipped cohort
note: mean places gained, 95% bootstrap CI [18.20, 24.48], 25 up / 0 down, exact sign test p = 5.96e-08. This interval is the *within-cohort* one: it holds these 100 candidates fixed and asks how precisely their mean movement is estimated. It is narrower than the across-seed interval above and answers a narrower question.

name: over_seller_places_lost
source: metrics.m10_stability — paired bootstrap on the shipped cohort
note: mean places lost, 95% bootstrap CI on the signed movement [-27.52, -21.52], 25 down / 0 up, exact sign test p = 5.96e-08. Demotion of over-sellers is the half of the correction that matters for fairness: promoting a hidden gem helps one candidate, demoting an over-seller is what stops the shortlist being wrong.

name: movement_direction_is_significant_for_both_planted_cases
note: exact binomial, ties discarded, no normal approximation. What the p-value does and does not say: it says the direction of movement is not a coin flip under this cohort. It says nothing about whether the planted errors resemble real resume inflation, which is an assumption of the generator and the central limitation of the whole audit.

name: within_cohort_and_across_seed_intervals_differ
note: across-seed 95% interval for τ-b gain is [0.3333, 0.4388] (width 0.1055); the within-cohort bootstrap holds the draw fixed and is necessarily tighter. Reported separately on purpose — quoting the tighter interval for the broader claim is the most common way a simulation result gets overstated, and it would be easy to do here by accident.

What is measured here is that the path exists and carries the candidate's verbatim answer; how often it fires needs a real run.

They are billed, they are charged against maxOutputTokens, and they never appear in the response body, so a token budget sized from the expected JSON is short by an amount the response does not reveal. A local model run without a reasoning phase does not carry this cost, which cuts the opposite way to the usual cloud-versus-local comparison. Measured live on 2026-09-24T12:54:19+00:00; replayed from live_provider_contract.json because this run had no live provider enabled.

name: shipped_budgets_complete_the_response
note: every probe finished with STOP at the max_output_tokens its production call site passes, so neither shipped budget truncates on a minimal input. Note the failure mode this rules out: a truncated reply still returns HTTP 200 with partial text, so it surfaces as a JSON parse error and a silent re-ask, not as a recognisable budget error. Measured live on 2026-09-24T12:54:19+00:00; replayed from live_provider_contract.json because this run had no live provider enabled.

name: gemini_reports_generation_time
note: the response carries promptTokenCount / candidatesTokenCount / thoughtsTokenCount but no server-side generation duration, so tokens-per-second cannot be computed for this provider without folding the network round trip into the denominator. LLMResult.eval_seconds is left None rather than filled from wall-clock. Measured live on 2026-09-24T12:54:19+00:00; replayed from live_provider_contract.json because this run had no live provider enabled.

name: real_model_is_fooled_by_resume_inflation
needs: whether a real screener scores an inflated resume above an honest one from the same competence band — the assumption every ranking result in this harness is built on. Costs 40 model calls, paced at one start every 6.5s to stay inside a free-tier rate limit (about 4 minutes): `METRICS_LIVE_PROVIDER=gemini .venv/Scripts/python -m metrics.run_all --only m11_live_screening`. Sends generated resume text only — no real candidate data exists in this project's throwaway database. Attempted on 2026-09-26 and not completed: the free-tier daily request allowance on both configured keys was exhausted partway through, and every remaining call returned HTTP 429. A 40-call validation run is therefore not reliably completable in one day on the free hosted tier — which is a measured argument for the local-Ollama path, not merely an inconvenience. Re-run with restored quota, or point LLM_PROVIDER at a local model.

name: model_inference_latency
needs: An Ollama run: `ollama pull llama3.1` then screen N applications with LLM_PROVIDER=ollama, recording p50/p95 per call alongside the model tag, quantisation, context length, CPU/GPU and peak RAM/VRAM. Without those five facts beside it a latency number is not a result. Report separately for screening (one long prompt) and interview turns (many short ones) — they have different shapes.

name: tokens_per_second
needs: Ollama returns prompt_eval_count, eval_count, prompt_eval_duration and eval_duration. llm/ollama.py already sums the two counts into LLMResult.tokens but drops both durations, which are the denominators. Keeping them would make throughput measurable with no new dependency — a small, worthwhile change, and the paper should not claim tokens/sec until it is made.

name: peak_ram_and_vram
needs: `ollama ps` during a run for model residency, plus psutil RSS sampling for the Streamlit process and nvidia-smi if a GPU is used. Relevant to the paper's deployability claim: the argument for local inference is that a hiring team can run it on hardware they own, and that argument needs a memory figure.
